extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literature; novelists and creative-writing learners
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing and applying E. M. Forster's lecture framework for looking at novels, which breaks novelcraft into discrete 'aspects' such as story, people, plot, fantasy, prophecy, and pattern/rhythm. Useful for literary analysis and for novelists thinking about their craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the 'aspects of the novel' that Forster discusses as a way to look at novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the page: this is part of a series of lectures in which Forster 'discusses both the different ways we can look at a novel and the different ways a novelist can look at his work.' 'The aspects of the novel Forster discusses are the story, people, plot, fantasy, prophecy and rhythm.' The entry on 'Story' is presented as a distinct analytical dimension to evaluate a novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: People
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the distinctive aspects Forster treats — the characterization or people in a novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among Forster's aspects: 'story, people, plot, fantasy, prophecy and rhythm.' The recording includes two tracks for 'People' ('III People' and 'IV People (continued)'), indicating extended treatment of characterization as a core evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Forster's aspect focusing on the plot structure of a novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named explicitly in the summary as one of the aspects: 'story, people, plot, fantasy, prophecy and rhythm.' Treated as a separate analytical criterion distinct from 'story' and 'people.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Fantasy
rubrics_metrics.description: An aspect Forster discusses concerning elements of fantasy or imaginative invention within novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in the list of aspects on the page. Presented as one of the lenses through which to evaluate or think about novels in Forster's lectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy
rubrics_metrics.description: Forster's term for an aspect of the novel, likely relating to thematic vision, moral stance, or the novel's broader implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly named among the aspects on the catalog page ('story, people, plot, fantasy, prophecy and rhythm'). The page does not expand on the definition, but presents it as a discrete evaluative dimension in the lecture series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern and Rhythm
rubrics_metrics.description: The aspect concerned with patterning and rhythmic qualities in novels (sometimes shortened to 'rhythm').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the summary as 'pattern and rhythm' (also referenced as 'rhythm' elsewhere). Presented as one of the core aspects Forster examines in the lecture series; the page notes the work is an academic analysis but 'accessible and engaging.'
